ruling.recommended_action: Close the dispute: the $6.61 driver-cancellation no-show fee stands; no refund or waiver.
ruling.reasoning:
The fee at issue is the $6.61 cancellation fee, which under NS-0 is chargeable only through the named branches; here `cancelled_by = driver` and the driver's cancellation is based on an alleged rider no-show, so the case runs through NS-1/NS-2 [F4][F12][NS-0].

NS-1(i): the arrival confirmation is a driver tap ("I'm Here") at 17:19:15, not a platform auto-confirmation [F6]. NS-1(ii): at the moment of the tap the driver was 41 m from the pickup point, inside the 200 m radius (closest approach overall 35 m), so the button was pressed while actually at the pickup [F6][F1][NS-1].

NS-1(iii): after the tap the driver remained inside the 200 m radius continuously for 220 s (3 min 40 s) until cancelling at 17:22:55, exceeding the default threshold of more than 3 minutes (180 s) [F6][F4][NS-1]. The trace shows no GPS hole across the wait — samples run from the arrival confirmation to the cancellation without a gap beyond the hole threshold, and the driver was stationary at 54 m for the final 4 min 5 s [F2][F3][F6]. The driver's chat confirms the wait ("3 min up, cancelling the trip") and the rider produced no message of arrival or contact during the wait [F10][F9][F11]. The driver's after-the-fact statement is consistent and is corroborated by system records, which override statements in any case [F12][F6].

All three NS-1 conditions therefore hold, so the $6.61 rider cancellation fee is valid and no refund is due; the mirror-image NS-2 (any condition failing) does not apply [NS-1][NS-2].

Route-deviation clauses have no work to do here: the ride was cancelled before any movement to the destination, and there are no off-route segment facts; the traffic and weather records are clean but irrelevant to the no-show question [F13][F14][F15][RD-1]. Likewise FARE-1/FARE-2 are not engaged — the only charge is the published $6.61 cancellation fee and there is no toll field [F7][F8][FARE-1][FARE-2].

The rider's profile (no prior upheld no-show disputes) and the driver's profile (two prior upheld no-show disputes) cannot decide this case on their own; the outcome rests on the GPS and timeline records [F16][F17]. Because no RD-2 refund arises and no RD-1 violation is recorded, the profile-based account flag under RD-6 is not triggered [F6][RD-6]. The complaint was filed within the NS-7 window and would only have mattered for payout form had a fee been waived [NS-7].

Amount: no money is returned. The fee on record is $6.61 [F7][F4]; NS-1 makes it payable, so the refundable amount is $0.00 (no arithmetic rate applies because NS-1, not RD-2, governs) [NS-1][RD-2].

The only rider assertion — coming out 'a minute' after the cancellation — is immaterial: NS-1(iii) is measured from the arrival confirmation to the cancellation, and the record shows 220 s inside the radius after the driver_tap at 17:19:15 with the cancellation at 17:22:55, already past the 3-minute threshold before the rider emerged [F6][F4][NS-1].
